notes.title: inKONBINI: Prologue Demo is Out Now!
notes.notes:
We’re thrilled to finally share the very first playable demo of inKONBINI with you!

Available now on Steam, the inKONBINI: Prologue Demo invites you into the cozy world of a small-town Honki-Ponki convenience store. Play as Makoto Hayakawa, meet your first customer, and begin your journey of discovery in a world where every interaction matters.

We hope you enjoy this small slice of the game, and that you’ll keep looking forward to what’s to come. In the meantime, please help us spread the word about inKONBINI on social media during LudoNarraCon 2025. 

Your support means the world to us! 

Team Nagai

notes.title: inKONBINI: Prologue Demo is arriving May 1st!
notes.notes:
We’re thrilled to announce that the first-ever playable demo of [i]inKONBINI: One Store. Many Stories[/i] will be available next week, arriving on Steam May 1!
 
Presented as part of [b]LudoNarraCon 2025[/b], this special [b]Prologue Demo[/b] offers a preview of the game’s opening chapter and a taste of what’s to come when the full game launches early next year.

Needless to say, releasing this demo is a big milestone for us at Nagai Industries. While we’ve had the joy of watching players interact with [i]inKONBINI[/i] at various offline events, bringing it to a global audience through a digital demo is both incredibly exciting, and honestly, a little terrifying.

This marks the very first time we’re letting the game speak entirely for itself, inviting you to immerse in its cozy world that we have crafted with care, love and passion. We've seen your anticipation for the game, and we’ve worked hard to ensure this demo delivers a polished, fine-tuned experience.

In the demo, you’ll play the very beginning of the game, as Makoto starts her first night shift at the Honki-Ponki convenience store. Everything feels calm and nostalgic here, from the vintage ’90s fridges to the chunky yellow tablets used by daytime staff, and the landline you can actually use to make phone calls.

Take your time getting to know the store and settling into its rhythm as you restock shelves, soak in the atmosphere, and wait for the first customer to arrive... But no spoilers for now!
 
Inspired in part by the Japanese philosophy of [i]ichi-go ichi-e[/i] — the belief that each encounter is unique and unrepeatable — we’ve chosen to make this Prologue Demo a limited-time experience. It will be [b]available from May 1 to May 8[/b] only, so please make a little room in your schedule to join us in this moment — brief, but hopefully unforgettable.
 
We truly hope you enjoy inKONBINI: Prologue Demo and the quiet joy of touching lives as a konbini clerk… and we’re looking forward to hearing your thoughts and feedback!

See you soon behind the counter!


Team Nagai

notes.title: inKONBINI at Day of the Devs
notes.notes:
Huh, we’re finally catching our breath after GDC — and especially after Day of the Devs!

It was a huge honor for us to showcase our game to so many people and open the doors of our konbini to a whole new audience.
Turns out the demo takes around 20–25 minutes to complete, so quite a few folks got to experience Makoto’s story firsthand!

We received so much wonderful feedback, so our main focus now is making the demo public — and doing it right, as soon as we can!

Big thanks to everyone who stopped by the event 💛
And for those who couldn’t meet us in person — get ready! Very soon, you’ll be able to join Makoto in her aunt’s little shop too! 🛍️

notes.title: inKONBINI: One Store. Many Stories is in Alpha, With a New Trailer Released!
notes.notes:
Good things take time… Many of you have been waiting for updates on development progress of inKONBINI ever since the game’s announcement in April this year. 

Today, the game’s new trailer has had its premiere at Day of the Devs: The Game Awards Edition 2024 curated by Double Fine and iam8bit, Inc.

We at Nagai Industries are immensely proud to have inKONBINI featured among the most anticipated indie titles from all over the world, and as we’ve been quietly working on the game over the past eight months, now we feel the time is right to share with you some news.

The first order of things for us is to let you know that inKONBINI has reached an Alpha stage. It’s a really important development milestone, which means we have the game playable (still, not all of the episodes planned for release, but a large portion of them), all the core functionality is in place, as well as all the main story beats.

We often get asked what kind of experience inKONBINI will have to offer when it’s released and in what proportions the elements of simulation and narrative-driven adventure are mixed? 

The truth is every game tells you what it wants to be, and if you listen carefully, it organically evolves into something unique and authentic. inKONBINI was conceived as a job simulation game, so for a long time we considered a simulation part to be the main pillar, therefore putting a lot of effort into making store management mechanics as smooth and intuitive as possible.

But as we kept working on the story elements, the characters started coming to life, and gradually we came to realise that the heart and soul of the game are really in player’s interaction with the customers, and at the same time that this is what makes the game stand out from the crowd of simulation-focused titles.

So, when it comes to genre definition, inKONBINI is a narrative-focused experience with simulation elements that are accessible and satisfying, but not overwhelmingly complex.

If we did our job right with the game’s announcement teaser, you might have already seen glimpses of the game’s elements and how they blend together, but in this new trailer we try to tell in a bit more straightforward way what the game is and how it’s going to be felt when you play it.

We hope you enjoyed watching the new trailer (if you haven’t yet, it’s right down below) and that you are excited to learn more about inKONBINI in the coming months.

[previewyoutube=E37Ajl5C2vY;full][/previewyoutube] 

Apart from the Day of the Devs trailer premiere, we also have a brand-new website ready to check out! Follow the link to experience inkonbini.com


If you’re active on Discord, join our community right here: https://discord.gg/N5UYkHXm


And follow inKONBINI on other social media channels that are going to burst with new information about the game very soon!

And this is all for now... Please, stay tuned for new updates, and thank you for your continued support!

Team Nagai

notes.title: Big Idea and the Importance of Making It Right — Dev Diary #1
notes.notes:
There is no single way to design a video game, but no matter what the genre, gameplay, or visual style is, it all starts with an idea. Finding a good one that will spark everyone’s imagination, will be able to sustain the team’s creative energy for long enough, and will appeal to a playing audience, is a tricky business. Especially when it’s your first game.

In fact, it’s very rare in any creative field, when the first try on a concept turns out to be the one that provides all the necessary elements for the final product. In the best case scenario, you’ll have a kernel of an idea that would be developed and elaborated upon through many stages of work before being realised in the form that looks solid, finished, and right.

This quality of rightness is arguably more important than anything else in game development as it defines how well every single element of the experience serves its purpose and complements the whole. It brings story, gameplay, animation, UI, controls, visuals, sounds, and music to a common denominator resulting in an overall impression that players will be getting from the game.

So, you can say that this ephemeral thing called a game concept is a compilation of ideas and elements that fit together in a way that is novel and compelling to be considered worthwhile. And we were on the search for a great one when we first started thinking of the game that would become [b]inKONBINI[/b].

From the very beginning, we knew our internal resources were limited, so we had to scope the project accordingly. Early on, we made a decision to build the whole game around a single location that would allow for a lot of gameplay interactions, have a unique narrative flavor, and also this feeling of ease that we all enjoyed playing our favorite cozy titles.

They say constraints will serve you well, and that’s definitely been true in our case. As you can see, we didn’t have a genre or particular style in mind from the outset, but instead were driven by production limitations. In a series of blueprint sessions, we went through a number of locations and settings, trying to imagine various gameplay scenarios that could occur in those environments. 

In a parallel universe, we could have ended up with a game set on a steam boat, a gas station, or a farm, but none of those struck a particular impression as we were toying with them, throwing dozens of ideas on the wall. 

It’s always kind of a miracle when one of them sticks, because you can feel it right away, and that’s what happened when we stumbled upon a Japanese convenience store as our potential setting. Just like many good things, a konbini has always been there, right in front of our eyes, as a place that we went to daily to get some snacks, use an ATM, and do plenty of things that instantaneously materialized as gameplay activities and situations in our game design oriented brains.

Someone suggested an idea to go back in time and explore the opportunities that the non-digitised early 1990s offered in terms of mood and feel as well as gameplay variety. For all of us on the team, that time period has always been special in how we remember it and coloured brightly with our childhood memories, so this take on the concept felt natural and was accepted by everyone.

That way, the initial concept put in the context of the early 1990s suddenly felt right, felt like a dream game, or more like a game that should have already existed, but somehow hasn’t been made yet, and that’s become our privilege to discover it and make it real.

We were lucky to find our setting, but everything else was still unclear. Although it was natural to see players fill the shoes of a store clerk since the game was set in a konbini, Makoto Hayakawa didn’t exist as a central character at the time, and we didn’t have a slightest idea of her role in the story or any background for her.

As we went on trying to crystallize our vision, we took a lot of inspiration from a Japanese TV series [b]Tokyo Diner: Midnight Stories[/b] that you can now watch on Netflix. Despite being much more mature in tone, the show had a narrative style that we felt would fit our game. Instead of making the owner a protagonist in a traditional sense, it focused on individual stories of customers visiting the titular diner at night. This storytelling approach made perfect sense for us since it presented an opportunity to create a whole canvas of a small-town life, with all the intricate connections between customers coming to the store, without us ever leaving the store itself.

A list of references that we had put together to define the mood and aesthetics of the game included notable [b]Studio Ghibli[/b] animated movies, like [b]Only Yesterday (1991)[/b] and [b]Whisper of the Heart (1995)[/b], but also featured a selection of contemporary independent drama with [b]Paterson (2016)[/b] and [b]Rent-a-Cat (2012)[/b] heading the list. Although being varied and seemingly different from one another, they all focused on minutiae of everyday life and made a commentary on how some of its calmest moments could be the most beautiful and fulfilling. 

Another recent cinematic work that would have made it to our reference list had it been released a year earlier is Wim Wenders’ instant classic [b]Perfect Days (2023)[/b], a poignant picture celebrating the moments of serenity found in the ordinary routine of a quiet Tokyo public toilets cleaner. The only thing that can be said here without the risk of spoiling either the movie or our own story content is that on a concept level it’s very close to what we have aspirations for inKONBINI to achieve through its meditative gameplay.

Many of you have already pointed at [b]Lake (2021)[/b] as a video game title that feels somewhat similar to our project in how it puts interactive story first providing a calming experience and the world you want to inhabit. And we certainly aren’t shying away from being compared to one of our main inspirations here. Gamious production has graciously paved the road for other developers to explore how non-violent, meaningful, and accessible interactive content can be made and presented in the current gaming landscape, and we’re just proud to see our brief teaser trailer inspire players to make this kind of connection.

The last, but probably the most important element that would shape the game concept for us was a unique vibe that we wanted our game to evoke. As we kept exchanging ideas on what kind of interactive experiences we found the most memorable, it became clear to us that some of our favorite titles resonated with the playing community on the merits of mood and atmosphere first and foremost. 

While gameplay and visuals are almost always meant to be refined and polished, the way how the game feels doesn’t necessarily get the same amount of time and attention. Partly because tuning up a tangible and correct atmosphere is a very delicate matter, but when done right it really can become a solid foundation for the whole experience, so we made it our priority right from the beginning.

These four elements — a [b]Japanese convenience store[/b] as a cozy and familiar location, [b]the 1990s[/b] as a nostalgic time period, a [b]multi-character narrative[/b] structure, and [b]a quiet, tranquil, and peaceful atmosphere[/b]  — became the cornerstones of the experience we set out to create. 

There were still more questions than answers about what kind of game inKONBINI would be when it’s out, and many important things regarding gameplay and story were yet to be specified (see, we didn’t even have a title for the game!), but we had a groundwork that felt concrete, well-designed, and strong enough to sustain all the narrative cargo and gameplay functionality that we were about to put atop of it.

The idea was there, we only needed to find ways to bring it to fruition…

Let us know in the comments what other [b]movies, books, and video games[/b] you can think of that would make it into our list of references and stir the feelings of calm and relaxation.

notes.title: 40,000 players wishlisted inKONBINI in the first four weeks!
notes.notes:
It’s been a little over a month since we announced [b]inKONBINI: One Store. Many Stories[/b]™ with a teaser trailer giving you a first glimpse of the game we’ve been working on quietly for a year.

To keep things under wraps for such a long time, and then to be able to see all the love and anticipation the game has been met with — honestly, nothing even comes close, and we at [b]Nagai Industries[/b] are humbled by this kind of reception from players all over the world.

The amount of exposure inKONBINI™ has received throughout gaming media in the first weeks since the announcement has been instrumental in spreading the word and growing our community, but it’s your willingness to discover the game on Steam and to share your feedback that’s given us confidence it’s all been worth the efforts.

Now, we would like to express our sincerest gratitude to all of you for supporting our vision of a relaxing narrative-based simulation game and to share our excitement about the fact that inKONBINI™ has been [b]wishlisted on Steam Store by more than 40,000 players[/b] as we’re writing this.

This kind of recognition means a lot for an independent game studio developing its debut title. That’s why we would like to take this moment to thank you all for your support and to let you know that we are determined to deliver the best-quality interactive experience for you to enjoy when the game is released early next year.

We are really excited to share more about inKONBINI: One Store. Many Stories™ in the coming months and will do our best to keep you up to date with the game’s development progress from this point on.

Please, stay tuned — great things are ahead!
